explanation: Son of King David and Maaka, who rebels against his father and seizes the throne in Jerusalem.
The second king of Israel, known for his skill as a warrior, musician, and poet. He is the author of many psalms.
A Benjamite who led a rebellion against King David after Absalom's death.
A member of Saul's family who cursed and threw stones at David while he fled from Absalom.
David's friend and advisor, sent back to Jerusalem to spy on Absalom and give him bad advice.
Former advisor to David who betrays him and supports Absalom in his rebellion.
Servant of Mephibosheth, Saul's grandson, who provides David with food and drink during his flight from Jerusalem.
Grandson of King Saul and son of Jonathan, accused by Ziba of betraying David.
The Almighty Creator who, according to Genesis, created the heavens, the earth, and all life.
